Praktik PC BIOS, version 2.18-19

Complete disassembly with a comment on every line. The 1992 C.S.T. version with the LANcom Network Remote Loader 1.2 instead of the cassette loader.

Important. The Praktik motherboard power connector looks like the standard IBM PC 5.25-inch floppy drive power connector, BUT(!) its pinout does not match the standard one. Connecting a standard IBM PC power supply burns out the chips on the motherboard. Check the pinout before applying power.
4385 instructions4974 listing linesCPU 8088/8086"probably" = inferred from code

Version 2.18-19_new: network boot

This is the 1992 C.S.T. version (based on 2.16-17) in which INT 18h runs the network loader "LANcom Network Remote Loader. Version 1.2 (C) C.S.T. Co., 1992" instead of the cassette loader. The loader occupies the free part of segment F400 (F400:0C4F–162B). Lines identical to 2.16-17 carry the same comments; the architecture is described on the 2.16-17 page.

Changes in the main BIOS

  • The INT 18h vector is F400:0C4F (set at F000:E3C7). The machine falls back to network boot if there is no ROM BASIC, if there is no floppy drive (E450), and if booting from floppy fails (INT 19h, E724).
  • Network boot with the Del key. At the start of the memory test POST sets 0040:0071 = 20h ("POST in progress"). Pressing Del at that moment makes the keyboard handler (EA13) set bit 6. The rest of the memory test is then skipped (wrapper E45C), and POST calls INT 18h right away (E3D4) without touching the floppy drives.
  • The tape loader is still in ROM (old_tape_loader_unused, F000:E4A2), but nothing references it any more. The message «Ошибка загрузки программы» ("Program load error") is shortened to «Ошибка загрузки» ("Load error").
  • The model byte at F000:FFFE changes from FFh (IBM PC) to FDh (the code IBM used for the PCjr), and the checksum padding byte becomes F4h.

Network hardware

There is no separate network adapter: the network runs over the second 8250 serial port (COM2, registers F000:0DF0–0DFE) on a shared half-duplex line, probably RS-485.

  • Speed: divisor 1, i.e. the maximum — 115200 baud with a 1.8432 MHz crystal. 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit.
  • The station number 0–15 is read from F000:0DE0 (low 4 bits), probably from jumpers on the board.
  • The DCD line (MSR bit 7) probably signals that the line is busy; RTS enables the transmitter.
  • The loader installs its own INT 0Ch handler (F400:132E); its work area is segment 9000h.

Frame format

16h 16h 16h 16h | destination | source | 01 | length (2 bytes) | header checksum | data | data checksum | 04h

  • The checksums make the byte sum zero. Data is at most 240h bytes. Destination F9h is broadcast.
  • Line access. A station waits for the line to become free, then waits a delay that depends on its number and enables the transmitter. It listens to its own first bytes: if the echo does not match there was a collision, and the transmission is retried with a longer delay.
  • Receive. The whole frame is received inside one interrupt; the bytes are parsed by a state machine (F400:138F onward). The received frame is stored at 9000:0071.

Boot protocol

The frame data begin with a 30-byte IPX-format header (checksum FFFFh, length, 6-byte nodes, socket 0454h). It is followed by the LANcom transport header: packet type (2 — name query, 4 — session request, 7 — data, 8 — acknowledge, 0Dh/0Eh — disconnect), connection and packet numbers, message length and fragment offset. An SMB message comes last.

1. First, up to 3 requests to station F8h (sub_0EAA). If it answers, it can write a ready image straight into the station's memory. This is probably a mode where the teacher's machine in a classroom pushes the boot image. 2. Broadcast query for the name SERVER, up to 30 attempts. If nobody answers: "Server Not Found." and INT 18h again. 3. Session request from the name STATION_x, where x = '@' + station number. 4. SMB exchange: Negotiate with the "PC NETWORK PROGRAM 1.0" dialect, Tree Connect to \\SERVER\RLOAD, Open \NETBOOT.@@@. If the file is missing: "Remote Loading File Not Found." 5. The file is read in blocks of 1FD0h bytes into memory starting at 6000:0000, then Close, Tree Disconnect and disconnect. 6. "MS/DOS Loading ...". INT 13h is replaced by the handler at F400:0F50 — a RAM disk for drive A: (8 sectors per track, one side, segment = 6000h + sector number × 20h, write-protected). The boot sector is read to 0000:7C00 and control passes to it, just like a normal floppy boot.

Likely bugs in the code

  • The Close request does not fill in the file ID (FID), and the Read request puts the FID into the "remaining" field instead of a count.
  • The high byte of the baud divisor is written to F000:0DF1 instead of the DLM register (0DF2).
  • A received frame with exactly 240h data bytes overwrites the station number in the work area.
  • Repeated INT 18h calls after errors do not unwind the stack.

Sources

  • The BIOS files were taken from the post «Журнал восстановления Практика» ("Praktik restoration log") on the zxdesu site, 2016: https://zxdesu.byethost32.com/2016/07/28/%d0%b6%d1%83%d1%80%d0%bd%d0%b0%d0%bb-%d0%b2%d0%be%d1%81%d1%81%d1%82%d0%b0%d0%bd%d0%be%d0%b2%d0%bb%d0%b5%d0%bd%d0%b8%d1%8f-%d0%bf%d1%80%d0%b0%d0%ba%d1%82%d0%b8%d0%ba%d0%b0/
  • Description of the Praktik computer (PK8641) on retro-computer.ru: https://retro-computer.ru/item/PRAKTIK-PK8641.html

Segment F400 — peripheral emulator (first 8 KB of ROM)

port_index_table — maps port number (000–3FF) to an offset into the NMI handler table.
Index = bits 0–9 of latch F000:0200; byte = 2*handler number in nmi_port_handlers (F400:049F).
Value 52h (handler #41 nmi_port_unused) — port not emulated: writes ignored, reads return FFh.
NMI_HANDLER reads word cs:[bx] from here and clears the high byte, i.e. only this byte is used.

INT0F_IRQ_DISPATCH — common hardware interrupt handler (vector INT 0Fh), replaces the 8259.
Reads the request register F000:0200 (high byte): bit 15 — floppy (INT 0Eh), bit 14 — timer (INT 08h),
bit 13 — keyboard (INT 09h), bit 12 — COM1 (INT 0Ch). One source is serviced per entry, by priority.
Special case: floppy IRQ during programmed FDC data transfer (0040:00B9 bit 3 = 0) — the stack
is cut back to the return address into NMI_HANDLER, i.e. the transfer loop in nmi_port_3F5 is aborted.

NMI_HANDLER — NMI handler (vector INT 2): software emulation of IBM PC I/O ports.
Hardware traps IN/OUT and raises NMI. F000:0200 — latch: bits 0–9 = port number,
bit 10 = 1 on write (OUT), 0 on read (IN); bit 11 = NMI caused by port access.
F000:0400/0401 — OUT data (even/odd bus byte). Handler is called with ZF=1 on IN,
ZF=0 on OUT, AX = latch, ES = F000, BP → frame: [bp]=program's AX (IN result goes here).
NMI_HANDLER:
F400:046C06push esSave ES (frame: [bp+6])

F400:046E53push bxSave BX ([bp+2])
F400:046F50push axSave interrupted program's AX ([bp+0] — handler writes IN result here)

F400:047CF6C708test bh, 8Bit 11: NMI caused by I/O port trap?

F400:04818BC3mov ax, bxAX = copy of latch (handlers test bits 10/11 in AH)

F400:04872E8B1Fmov bx, word cs:[bx]Fetch byte from port_index_table (F400:0000+port)

F400:0494FFD3call bxCall emulated port handler
loc_0496: ← 047F

write ×0.83809 (D68Dh/10000h). Low/high byte flip-flop — 0040:00A6, word buffer — 0040:00A8/00A9.

INT18_NET_LOADER — network loader «LANcom Network Remote Loader 1.2» (C.S.T., 1992); INT 18h vector = F400:0C4F (set at F000:E3C7).
Called from POST: Del during the memory test (E3E0), no floppy drive (E450), INT 19h failure (E724).
Network adapter — 8250 COM2 (F000:0DF0–0DFE), IRQ via INT 0Ch (F400:132E); station number — F000:0DE0 & 0Fh.
Wire frame: 16h 16h 16h 16h, dst, src, 01, length (word), header checksum, data, data checksum, 04h (sub_11BF/sub_1221).
Data: IPX-like header 9000:000A–0027 (FFFF, BE length, networks/nodes/sockets 0454h), control fields 0028–0033, SMB from 9000:0034.
Work area 9000h: 0000 — transmit buffer, 0071 — receive buffer (first 60h bytes copied to 0004), 02B6–02DA — variables.
Sequence: receive image from station F8h (sub_0EAA) → find «SERVER» → connect «STATION_x» → SMB NEGPROT, TCON \\SERVER\RLOAD,
EXIT, OPEN \NETBOOT.@@@, READ×N into 6000:0000, CLOSE, TDIS → disconnect → INT 13h = RAM disk F400:0F50 → jmp 0000:7C00.
Never returns; on failure — message, restore INT 0Ch and re-issue INT 18h (endless restart).

sub_0EAA — "push" mode: image sent by another station. Writes SYN preamble 16h×4 to 9000:0000.
Up to 3 times sends a 5-byte service frame to address F8h (probably the control station/server) (000E = 0 — request).
If F8h answers — receives data frames: far destination address 002E:0030 (offset:segment), length 0032,
data at 9000:00A1 — copies them to memory; on receive error sends a retransmit request (000E = FFh).
Final 5-byte frame (sender ≠ own station) → 9000:02BC = FFh. Timeout/no reply — just return.

sub_0F50 — RAM disk INT 13h (vector set at 0E8C). Floppy image at 6000:0000, 8 sectors per track,
head DH ignored: logical sector = CH*8 + CL − 1, segment = 6000h + sector*20h (probably a 160 KB image).
DL ≠ 0 → CF=1, AH unchanged. AH=0,1,4 → AH=0, CF=0. AH=2 → read AL sectors to ES:BX, AH=0.
AH=3,5 → AH=3 "write protected", CF=1. AH>5 (incl. 8) → CF=1. Exits via RETF 2 — flags passed to caller.

Entry: DS = F000h, ES = 9000h. 1) wait until DCD (MSR bit 7) drops — line free;

INT0C_NET — INT 0Ch interrupt handler for the network channel 8250 (F000:0DF0–0DFE, "COM2" ports).
Installed by sub_1434 in place of the COM1 handler; probably called by the common INT 0Fh dispatcher.
IIR = 0 (modem status change): if DCD dropped — end of another station's frame: IER = 1, flush RBR.
IIR = 4 (byte received): first byte (SYN) discarded, then in a loop polling LSR.DR each byte
is passed to the receive state machine [2BFh] (ES = 9000h, CL = flag/checksum, DI = write pointer)
until it refuses (ZF=0) or DCD drops; then the state machine is reset to 138Fh. The whole frame is received
within a single interrupt. Other IIR values ignored. No EOI needed (no 8259).

INT 14h — serial port (standard IBM address E739, code identical to IBM XT BIOS).
In: AH = function (0 init, 1 send, 2 receive, 3 status), AL = parameters/character, DX = port number.
Base address taken from 0040:0000+2*DX; accesses to 8250 ports (3F8–3FF/2F8–2FF) are trapped by NMI and emulated.
Out: AH = line status (LSR), AL = MSR / received character; AH bit 7 = timeout.

INT 13h — floppy disk service (standard IBM entry point F000:EC59).
Functions: 0 reset, 1 status, 2 read, 3 write, 4 verify, 5 format, 8 drive parameters.
Input: AH=function, AL=sector count, CH=cylinder, CL=sector, DH=head, DL=drive (0–1), ES:BX=buffer.
Output: AH=status (0040:0041), CF=1 on error, AL=sectors processed.
765 controller (ports 3F2/3F4/3F5) and 8237 DMA channel 2 (ports 04/05/0A/0B/0C/81) — emulated via NMI.
Frame: [bp]=DX,[bp+2]=BP,[bp+4]=DI,[bp+6]=SI,[bp+8]=DS,[bp+0Ah]=CX,[bp+0Ch]=BX.

sub_EF65 — receive result bytes from floppy controller (NEC 765 result phase).
Reads up to 7 bytes from data port 3F5 into 0040:0042–0048 (ST0,ST1,ST2,C,H,R,N), polling MSR (3F4).
Output: CF=0 — success; CF=1 — error, 0040:0041 gets bit 80h (timeout) or 20h (controller failure).
Preserves CX, DX, BX; DS=0040. Ports 3F4/3F5 are emulated via NMI (765 emulation).

sub_EFAA — count sectors actually transferred after an INT 13h operation.
Input: CH = requested cylinder, CL = starting sector; DS=0040, result bytes at 0040:0042–0048.
If the controller stayed on the same cylinder: AL = R(next sector) − CL;
otherwise (ran past end of track): AL = EOT+1 − CL (EOT from INT 1Eh parameter table).
Output: AL = sector count; clobbers AH, BX.

INT17_PRINTER — printer service (standard IBM entry point F000:EFD2).
Input: AH=0 — print character AL, AH=1 — initialize, AH=2 — read status; DX = printer number (0–2).
Output: AH = printer status (bits as in IBM: 80h not busy, 40h ACK, 20h out of paper, 10h selected, 08h error, 01h timeout).
Base port taken from 0040:0008+2*DX, timeout from 0040:0078+DX. Ports 378–37A are emulated via NMI (LPT emulation).

INT10_VIDEO — BIOS video service (standard IBM entry point F000:F065).
Saves ES,DS,DX,CX,BX,SI,DI; AX is popped before jumping to the handler.
On handler entry: DS=0040, ES=B800 (CGA video memory), AL = original AL, AH = current mode (0040:0049),
SI = 2*function. Functions ≥10h are ignored. All handlers exit via common epilogue F1B9.
